Reference image: ORIGINAL character idle sprite strip. Preserve its EXACT character identity, compact body proportions, colors, clothing and small dense hand-pixelled classic Chinese mobile RPG style. Do not use tall anime illustration proportions or modern glossy rendering.
Generate a NEW, COMPLETE four-direction walking sprite atlas. Square 1024x1024 transparent PNG. EXACT 4 columns x 4 rows, 16 full-body sprites, each 256x256 cell. All cells equal, no printed grid, no labels, no floor, no shadow. TRUE TRANSPARENT ALPHA.
Each character approximately 190 pixels tall; head crown at local y=45, support sole y=232, pelvis aligned local x=128. Row 1: strictly FRONT, south/down walk towards viewer, symmetric shoulders, eyes forward, no sideways three-quarter torso.
Row 2: strictly LEFT profile, nose screen left.
Row 3: strictly RIGHT profile, nose screen right.
Row 4: strictly BACK, north/up walk away, no visible face.

Anatomical left and right, correctly projected into each view. Distinct visible alternating boot positions, short relaxed strides, no running/kneeling/squatting. Front/back contact frames visibly alternate which boot extends toward the ground baseline. BOTH legs readable in every cell. Passing poses close feet, support leg straight. Same gait amplitude and same 4-phase timing for ALL directions. Feet contact fixed baseline. Head/torso stay registered, at most 1 logical pixel bob. Clothes move subtly. No warping weapon, changing face, shrinking, or rotation within rows.
Keep weapon consistent with reference, same anatomical hand in every view. No glow/effects. Export sprite atlas only.
Character: Young clean-shaven male, chestnut spiky hair, black/navy armor with gold trim, red cape, silver broad sword held low with both hands. Compact original sprite proportions, not oversized rounded shoulder plates.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this 4-column x 4-row transparent RPG sprite sheet. Preserve ALL upper-body pixel art, face, outfit, weapon, hair, palette, direction order and consistent compact scale. Only correct legs/boots and bottom hems for a real alternating four-key walk. Current column 1 and 3 repeat the SAME supporting foot, which is WRONG. Current front boots overlap into one central leg, WRONG.
MANDATORY columns for front row AND back row:
Column 1: TWO boots clearly separated left/right of body midline. Screen-LEFT boot is DOWN at ground line, screen-RIGHT boot is 12 source pixels HIGHER.
Column 2: BOTH boots next to one another, equally LOW on SAME ground line, separated by narrow transparent gap. Neutral upright legs.
Column 3: opposite column 1! Screen-RIGHT boot is DOWN at ground line, screen-LEFT boot is 12 source pixels HIGHER. Do NOT copy column 1's legs!
Column 4: BOTH boots next to one another, equally LOW on SAME ground line. Neutral upright legs.
For BOTH side-view rows, columns 1 and 3 show opposite anatomical legs in forward contact. Column 1 near leg is forward extended, far leg back; column 3 far leg is forward extended, near leg back. Darken far leg consistently so alternating overlap is visible. Columns 2 and 4 show close parallel legs and planted boots under pelvis, nearly neutral pose, NOT a lifted knee and not crouching. Smooth 1-2-3-4-1 walking loop.
Make lower robe/coat opening wide enough for TWO legs visible, no single center foot, no feet hidden by skirt. Keep torso totally fixed across columns. True transparent background, NO colored fringe or red/yellow cutout outline, NO shadow, NO labels. Whole 4x4 sheet remains same layout, all poses fully contained with clear transparent gutters. Pixel art, not smooth illustration.
